title: Comparative Analysis of Smart Cities in Global South Countries: Vitória (Brazil) and Kigali (Rwanda)
content: Traditionally dominated by technocentric paradigms formulated in Global North metropolises—characterized by high-cost infrastructures such as digital twins and dense IoT sensor networks—the discourse on smart urbanism frequently overlooks the budgetary constraints, distributive asymmetries, and structural bottlenecks ubiquitous in developing nations. To overcome this conceptual gap, this article investigates the constitutive frameworks of smart cities in the Global South through a comparative qualitative and epistemic analysis of two cities recognized for technological development aimed at improving citizens’ quality of life: Vitória (Brazil) and Kigali (Rwanda). Methodologically, the comparison is structured around two complementary dimensions: audited indicators and regional composite indices (e.g., Connected Smart Cities Ranking and Oxford Economics Global Cities Index) and the Triple Helix Model adapted to Frugal Innovation (TH-FI), tailored for urban ecosystems facing severe capital constraints. The analysis demonstrates that while Vitória has consolidated its status as a national benchmark through the deepening of institutional trust capital, public data integration in healthcare, and the debureaucratization of autonomous citizen services, Kigali has emerged on the African stage through top-down state alignment focused on fleet e-mobility, solar energy transition, and green urban infrastructure. The study concludes that urban smartness in the Global South does not stem from emulating futuristic skylines, but from the capacity to align digital transformation with primary social and infrastructural priorities.
